newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Roly to emerge from transition pains.
newsitem.headline: Roly to emerge from transition pains.

text.p: Roly International, a home decor firm, expects to resume previous profit levels after absorbing the costs of expansion and change of policies in some of its key markets, company officials said on Thursday.
"The rebound and recovery should be within 12 months. Based on the few months of this (financial) year, we've had a huge increase in orders," chairman Robert Wang told reporters at a briefing.
"I feel very comfortable we can rebound within this year, back to the normal level...the previous year's income," he said.
The group announced a 52.9 percent slip in net profit for the year ended April 1997 to US$7.75 million. Turnover rose to US$247.19 million from US$238.33 million.
In a statement, the company said its home decor business experienced a shift in market development and product strategy, while its licenced consumer products business expanded in China.
Group profitability fell during this transition period as resources were devoted to cope with the changes.
It said decline of craft sales to U.S. chain store Wal-Mart, a major customer, was sharper than expected.
Sales for the year fell 34 percent to US$39 million, and profits declined because operating costs were not reduced in time to counter the loss in sales revenue.
Roly also faced over-capacity and higher costs in its distribution infrastructure and operations due to a fall in overall sales.
But chief financial officer Kim Khoo said the company was on track for a turnaround because of realignment of U.S. and U.K. operations, which have been less profitable recently.
"We are sizing down manufacturing in our U.K. Christmas decorative products and beefing up marketing and distribution in Poland," Khoo said.
Roly will also begin to reap rewards from store expansions in Greater China, from opening 45 stores in Hong Kong and China.
Total sales increased to US$34 million compared to US$25 million last fiscal year. Profits were thinner only because sales had not come in and because of store-opening expenses.
Wang said future earnings would be driven by brands, higher-margin products and mid to upper-middle income clients.
"By year 2000, branded products will account for 30 percent of total turnover," he said.
Brands and a higher class of customer base will be used as a "second wing" to uplift the home decor business which currently relies on volume and mass merchandise markets.
